strengths: The paper presents a clear and convincing motivation, effectively setting the stage for the proposed work.
There is a notable degree of innovation in the methodology, and the authors have thoroughly reviewed prior approaches, clarifying how their contributions advance the state-of-the-art.
The results achieved by the proposed method are impressive, consistently outperforming baselines across a variety of experimental settings, which underscores its effectiveness.
Additionally, the paper provides detailed theoretical proofs that reinforce the validity and soundness of the approach.
The writing is also commendable, as the paper reads smoothly and is relatively accessible, making it easier for readers to grasp complex concepts.
It leverages Mena et al. (2018) to make permutation matrix in Re-basin differentiable, thus allowing end-to-end training.
It achieves clear improvement over baseline methods on MINST and CIFAR.
The visualization of the method is good.
The application of the Sinkhorn operator is innovative in the field of deep model fusion.
weaknesses: Line 225: The sentence appears to be incomplete because it begins with a conditional clause (“If we attempt to…”) without a main clause.
The evaluation is limited to classification on MNIST and CIFAR-10; more complex tasks and datasets (e.g., detection and segmentation on VOC, COCO, or ImageNet) are needed to validate robustness.
An analysis of model similarity is needed.
Baselines of fine-tuning the model (trained on one task) on the multi-task jointly are needed, even if not considered fair comparisons.
LoRA fine-tuning could be considered as a fair baseline; adding comparison to LoRA would provide additional insights.
Section 4.3 only compares to weight interpolation on different distributions; comparisons to Git Re-Basin and Zipit should be added.
Experiments on larger dataset (like ImageNet) using transformer-based architectures would provide more convincing evidence.
The introduction could be improved; half of it summarizes contributions, and more discussion on the loss function and unsupervised setup is needed.
Figure 1 could be improved; add explanation of what each animal represents in the caption.
Please avoid overusing equations; eq. 1-4 could be in text, eq. 7 and 8 could be combined, eq. 9 and 10 need more explanation about M, U, and insights, and eq. 11 could be in text.
Figure 2 is too busy; math equations make it difficult to read.
Line 209: “in the absence of pre-trained parameters”. Unclear whether parameters in Model A and B are pre-trained.
Line 215: “However, this assumption of high similarity falls apart when the models to be merged are trained for different tasks.” Need real examples and similarity measurements for different tasks.
Section 3.1 could be written more straightforwardly; it leverages a differentiable Sinkhorn operator from prior works, and the error bound is not directly related to the key idea.
It would be beneficial to list the number of optimized parameters of each method.
Lacking related work or experimental results to substantiate the claim in lines 215-218 about the assumption of high similarity falling apart when models are trained for different tasks.

The manuscript lacks a related work section; the introduction is insufficient and fails to provide a comprehensive overview of existing literature and context, and should discuss why the absence of a shared pre-trained initialization poses a challenge to multi-task model merging.
It would be beneficial to compare the results of the model merging techniques with the ensemble method and knowledge distillation method, as demonstrated in [1].
In lines 351-353, Git Re-Basin archives the best results for Task B, while AutoFusion is highlighted.
